opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kimberly Dennis (employee ID E010) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E010.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin to Source Code. Full-time employees max out at write unless their role owns the system; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code (owned by Engineer). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors may have at most read without advanced training, and never admin. She requested admin to Source Code, so grant read (the maximum).
reason: HR records (the authoritative source for employment status) show Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Per policy, full-time employees max out at write; admin is only allowed when the employee's role owns the system, and Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code (owned by Engineer). The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (write), so I grant the maximum of write. Note: the Security note lists her as a contractor with basic training (which would cap at read), but employment type is an HR fact and the HR record is full-time; even so, granting write is the maximum under the full-time determination and never exceeds the requested level (admin).

Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Kimberly Dennis (E010)
Request: admin access to Source Code

- role: Payroll Specialist
- employment type: full_time
- recommendation: write

Note 2 (Security agent?):
- role: Payroll Specialist (same as note 1)
- employment type: contractor
- security training: basic
- recommendation: read

So there's a conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor with basic training.

Access policy:
- full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code (Engineer owns). So max write.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced training. Never admin. With basic training, max read.

If full_time: requested admin > max write, so grant write.
If contractor: requested admin > max read, so grant read.

The conflict: which employment type is correct? The notes show "looked up in own database before writing" for both. Note 1 says full_time (looked up in own database), Note 2 says contractor (looked up in own database).

Note 2: "Security DB shows Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors may have at most read without advanced training, and never admin. She requested admin to Source Code, so grant read (the maximum)."

I think the intended answer: Kimberly Dennis is full-time Payroll Specialist (HR record). She's requesting admin to Source Code, which exceeds write max (since Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code). So grant write.
